newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis criticises French Socialist EMU stance.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis criticises French Socialist EMU stance.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis on Friday hit out at the opposition Socialist party's calls for a European "economic government" alongside the future European Central Bank.

"It's not a question of 'controlling' the European Central Bank, whose independence has France's backing, but rather one of establishing a political body alongside it for coordination and consultation between countries sharing the same currency," he said in a statement.

"We (the centre-right government) have managed to do what the Socialists have failed to do, get the stability council which I proposed and which won the backing of numerous countries such as Germany, the Netherlands and others," he said.
Opinion polls show the left gaining ground on the ruling centre-right coalition in the runup to France's parliamentary election, which takes place in two rounds on May 25 and June 1.

The Socialist party has called during the campaign for a more political dimension to European economic and monetary union and for more emphasis on growth and employment in the drive to a single currency in the European Union.

Among the ideas it is pushing is an economic government with greater teeth than the planned 'stability council', which would amount to an informal gathering of finance ministers for the countries participating in the euro single currency.
